> XVIII Jeff Legge reclined in a long cane chair on a lawn which stretched to the edge of a cliff. Before him were the blue waters of the Channel, and the more gorgeous blue of an unflecked sky. He reached out his hand and took a glass that stood on the table by his side, sipped it with a wry face and called a name pettishly. It was Lila who came running to his side. “Take this stuff away, and bring me a whisky-and-soda,” he said. “The doctor said you weren’t to have anything but lime juice.
